fixes.explanation: Right on it, baker. John says, “And do not begin to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’” (Luke 3:8). Having the right family name doesn't replace fruit. It's like saying my stamper is famous, so my cookies don't need to come out right.
That's it, friend. Luke 3:2 says the word of God came to John son of Zechariah in the wilderness. Tiberius, Pilate, Herod, Annas and Caiaphas are all named, and the word of God comes to John.

A city makes sense when you hear that many important names. But Luke 3:2 says the word of God came to John son of Zechariah in the wilderness. The verse says wilderness, not a city. I'd have picked a city too, and I used to live in a drawer.

Yes, friend. John preaches “…a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins…” (Luke 3:3). In that verse, repentance is the word that goes with forgiveness of sins. John also tells the crowds to produce fruit in keeping with repentance (Luke 3:8).
Dedication sounds like a fine word, friend. But Luke 3:3 says John preaches “…a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins…” The word the text gives is repentance, not dedication.
That's the one, friend. John says, “You brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?” (Luke 3:7). He says it to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him.

Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), is a big name, and I see why you went there. But in Luke 3:8, John tells the crowds not to say to themselves, “We have Abraham as our father.” Abraham is the name in the verse. Moses doesn't come up in this passage.

It's actually true, friend. John says, “For I tell you that out of these stones God can raise up children for Abraham.” (Luke 3:8). Stones, of all things. I'm still a little amazed, and I've seen some stubborn dough.
Yes, baker. John says, “…every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.” (Luke 3:9). The axe lies ready at the root. That's the picture John gives the crowds.

A second chance sounds nice, and in a story Jesus tells, someone asks to leave a fig tree for another year (Luke 13:8). But that's not John's picture here. In Luke 3:9, “…every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.”

True. John says, “…and whoever has food should do the same.” (Luke 3:11). Whoever has two tunics shares with him who has none, and whoever has food does the same. The tunics and the food get the same instruction.
That's right, friend. Luke 3:15 says the people “…were all wondering in their hearts if John could be the Christ.” The verse says they were waiting expectantly. John's about to answer them straight.
I wish it had gone that way, friend. The crowds, the tax collectors, and the soldiers all asked John that question. But Luke 3:20 tells what Herod did: “He locked John up in prison.”
